questions.prompt: Which possessive marker indicates singular proper noun ownership (e.g. 'Maria's house')?
questions.explanation: 'Ni' is the singular proper noun possessive marker (e.g. ang bahay ni Maria = Maria's house).

questions.prompt: Which possessive marker indicates common noun ownership (e.g. 'the child's toy')?
questions.explanation: 'Ng' is the common noun possessive marker (e.g. ang laruan ng bata = the child's toy).

questions.prompt: In Tagalog possessive phrases, which element comes FIRST in sentence order?
options: The possessed object (e.g. ang bahay ni Maria)
The owner of the object (e.g. ni Maria ang bahay)
questions.correct_answer: The possessed object (e.g. ang bahay ni Maria)
questions.explanation: In Tagalog possessive constructions, the possessed object ALWAYS precedes the owner: 'ang bahay ni Maria' (the house of Maria).

questions.prompt: Which pair represents the 1st person singular 'my / mine' in Pre-Noun (with ligature) vs Post-Noun form?
questions.explanation: 'Akin' is used pre-noun (e.g. aking bahay), while 'ko' is used post-noun (e.g. bahay ko).

questions.prompt: Translate 'your book' using the post-noun possessive pronoun: 'libro ___'. ______
questions.explanation: 'Mo' is the 2nd person singular post-noun possessive pronoun ('libro mo' = your book).

questions.prompt: Which post-noun possessive pronoun means 'his' / 'her' / 'hers' (e.g. 'ang bahay ___')?
questions.explanation: 'Niya' is the 3rd person singular post-noun possessive pronoun ('his/her').

questions.prompt: Which demonstrative possessive word means 'of this person / object' (near speaker)?
questions.explanation: 'Nito' means 'of this' (near speaker, e.g. ang bahay nito).

questions.prompt: Which possessive marker is used before multiple proper names of people ('___ Maria at Pedro')? ______
questions.explanation: 'Nina' is the plural proper noun possessive marker (e.g. ang bahay nina Maria at Pedro).
